A [[Color|turquoise]]-plated<ref name="Chapter 22 AD" /> '''protocol droid''' with yellow [[sensor]]s was present on the independent [[planet]] [[Plazir-15]] during the early [[New Republic Era]].<ref name="Chapter 22" /> In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{MandoDate|22}}</ref> the [[protocol droid]] was a patron in the [[droid]]-exclusive [[cantina]], [[The Resistor]], and stood on a table together with a yellow [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]], two [[B1-series battle droid]]s and another droid near the entrance door. When the [[Mandalorian]]s [[Din Djarin]] and [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] entered the cantina during their [[Mission to Plazir-15|investigation]] of malfunctioning droids on Plazir-15, the protocol droid stared with all other droids at the two [[human]] interlopers and followed them with it's gaze as they walked to the counter, before it turned back around. When Djarin threatened [[Unidentified bartender droid (Plazir-15)|the bartender droid]], the protocol droid tried to walk to the door, but stopped when Djarin saw it and said that nobody would leave and instead walked back to it's table and continued to stare at the two humans.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

{{Droid-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The protocol droid first appeared in "[[Chapter 22: Guns for Hire]]," the sixth episode of the [[The Mandalorian Season Three|third season]] of the live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', which was directed by [[Bryce Dallas Howard]]<ref name="Chapter 22" /> and released on [[April 5]], [[2023]].<ref name="Writers Guild">{{WebCite|url=https://directories.wga.org/project/1185542/the-mandalorian|text=The Mandalorian|work=[https://www.wga.org wga.org]|archivedate=20221204123657}}</ref> In the episode the droid was physically portrayed by [[Daniel Bohman]] and simply credited as "Blue Protocol Droid Performance Artist".<ref name="Chapter 22" /> The droid originated as a design for a original character called RG-255 by the [[Fanon|fan]] droid builder Pedge of the UK Droid Builders club. The design was then seen by [[Chris Bartlett]], who portrayed multiple droids in ''The Mandalorian'', and planed to secretly incorporate the droid's design into the series. Although Pedge himself died before the release of the episode.<ref name="Darren Briscoe">{{Facebook|url=posts/pfbid02xdetHYxGuc5fAJSpoyMw4EEgaizvgHD8tJMSof8JLPJzcFJYUSkYNUnpHtXUWAuSl|username=darren.briscoe.7|name=Darren Briscoe|date=2023-04-06|quote=This is really special.... In the latest episode of 'The Mandalorian Chapter 22: Guns for hire' on Disney + there's a beautiful chrome blue protocol droid called RG-255. My pal from the UK Droid Builders club, Pedge, who had his own wonderfully accurate C-3P0 costume had designed the colouring and the name of a droid he wanted to build. Being in the Star Wars community this was seen by Chris Bartlett one of the droid actors on the show who was taken by this unique look. Plans were secretly made to incorporate the design into the show.Pedge had Motor Neurone disease and sadly died before he got to see his creation on-screen. This is such a wonderful tribute to his memory! Thanks to Pedge's wife Sonja for allowing me to share this X|archivedate=20260110195924}}</ref>

The unofficial action figure designer HasNoTalent later created a "[[Kenner Products|Kenner]] inspired" action figure of RG-255 which was sold together with signed autograph cards from Bohman. The figure's packaging also described RG-255 as being made from "legendary" durable "Blue Carbiltium alloy" sourced "from the mines of Tuuclae" and that he came from unknown origins before his memory was wiped when he was reprogrammed for his service on Plazir-15, but that his durable material "suggests a past as an interpreter for elected officials or military, or possibly service in dangerous industrial environments."<ref name="hasnotalent">{{Instagram|url=p/Cv5AN6iu1-F|username=hasnotalent|date=2023-08-13|quote=RG-255 Blue Protocol droid played by Daniel Bohman @danielbohman_art . These are in a new, digitally matched, screen accurate color! The 4th picture has the new screen accurate color on the left side which recreates RG-255's Blue Carbiltium alloy sourced from the mines of Tuuclae! 💙 3.75 inch scale with vintage style 5poa and will come in a resealable clam shell with custom card. Each card will be autographed and personalized by Daniel Bowman himself!|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/mkdIF}}</ref> Neither RG-255's name, pronouns or his past or material were mentioned in any official sources.
